title: Priv EKS provisioner: declarative init wizard and upgrade sentinel
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and an accompanying declarative initialization helper (init wizard) to provision Redwood Private EKS control planes in customer VPCs. This work bundles idempotent provisioning, preflight validation, KMS-integrated secrets bootstrap, cross-account IAM primitives, and an upgrade sentinel that gates control plane rolling upgrades with health checks and canary verification. The goal is to provide operators and solutions engineers a safe, repeatable path to stand up control planes with auditability and self-healing hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives in terraform/modules/private_controlplane and supports param-driven idempotent apply
Init wizard (CLI) can run preflight checks and generate a minimal tfvars file for common customer patterns
Preflight validates VPC subnets, route table NAT/IGW config, KMS key policies, S3/LB endpoints, and required API quotas
Upgrade sentinel performs canary scale-ups on a single AZ, runs health probes (API, kubelet, cert rotation), and aborts on regressions
All resources are tagged with org and environment metadata and emit logs to the platform audit sink
Module integrates with customer KMS (cross-account key support) and stores bootstrap secrets encrypted in SSM or S3 with proper IAM roles
Documented rollback strategy and runbook for failed upgrades included in docs/design
Automated acceptance tests run in CI using a lightweight kinD-based validator plus a small EKS smoke namespace in staging
tasks: Design module interface and variables (networking, kms, iam, tags, controlplane sizing)
Implement Terraform resources and export outputs for console and operators
Build init wizard (Go CLI) that runs dry-run preflights and emits tfvars
Add preflight remote checks (API reachability, quota checks, DNS, TCPSocket probes)
Implement upgrade sentinel Lambda + SQS orchestrator for staged rollouts
Write CI pipelines: lint, fmt, terraform validate, unit tests, and an integration smoke job
Author runbook and design doc, include rollback and escalation steps
Security review and KMS policy verification with Security team
